name: Live Connections Skip The Startup Mutex

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Live Connections Skip The Startup Mutex Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

Every batch a `connect()` subscriber (and every keyed watch) receives locks its `StartupConnection` mutex to learn that startup is over and read the snapshot version, long after startup. Publishing the live snapshot version in an atomic — stored under the mutex when the connection goes live, cleared under it on disposal — lets live batches skip the mutex; buffering and draining keep the locked path, so ordering and dedup against the snapshot are unchanged.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** atomic live-version fast path in `StartupConnection::receive`.
**Allowed changes:** `StartupConnection` in `crates/src/collections/connection.rs` (shared state struct, receive/start/disposal).
**Forbidden in this experiment:** signal values() startup, delivery queues, source publish paths.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Focused tests: `collections::tests::{connect_late_delivery,source_commit_order,suspension_versions,watch_batch_coalescing,sources,source_lock_policy}` and full lib + integration; clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` and `operator_updates` vs base, rerun borderline. Pass: cache-hot/update-connect >=5% faster; connect-per-iteration benches (live group, tree loads) not slower >10%.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

~5-10 ns less per connected batch.
